papers.title: Control of out-of-plane anti-damping spin torque with a canted ferromagnetic spin source
papers.authors: Xiaoxi Huang, Daniel A. Pharis, Hang Zhou, Zishen Tian, Thow Min Jerald Cham, Zhaoyang Wang, Yuhan Liang, Kyoungjun Lee, Yilin Evan Li, Maciej Olszewski, Di Yi, Chang-Beom Eom, Darrell G. Schlom, Lane W. Martin, Ding-Fu Shao, Daniel C. Ralph
papers.abstract: To achieve efficient anti-damping switching of nanoscale magnetic memories with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy using spin-orbit torque requires that the anti-damping spin-orbit torque have a strong out-of-plane component. The spin anomalous Hall effect and the planar Hall effect spin current produced by a ferromagnetic layer are candidate mechanisms for producing such an out-of-plane anti-damping torque, but both require that the magnetic moment of the spin source layer be canted partly out of the sample plane at zero applied magnetic field. Here we demonstrate such a canted configuration for a ferromagnetic SrRuO3 layer, and we characterize all vector components of the torque that it produces, including non-zero out-of-plane anti-damping torques. We verify that the out-of-plane spin component can be tuned by the orientation of the magnetic moment, with significant contributions from both the spin anomalous Hall effect and the planar Hall effect spin current. Huang et al. show that canted magnetization in SrRuO3 generates a sizable out-of-plane damping-like torque without relying on low crystal symmetry, offering a strategy toward scalable magnetic-memory devices with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy.
papers.summary_en: The study demonstrates that a canted SrRuO₃ ferromagnetic layer can generate an out-of-plane anti-damping spin-orbit torque. It identifies contributions from both the spin anomalous Hall effect and planar Hall effect spin current, and shows that the out-of-plane spin component can be tuned by changing the magnetic-moment orientation.

papers.physics_advance: Canted magnetization in SrRuO3 produces a tunable out-of-plane anti-damping torque, with contributions from both the spin anomalous Hall effect and planar Hall effect spin current.
papers.relevance_reason: This experimental study investigates magnetic spin transport in ferromagnetic SrRuO3 and identifies mechanisms that generate a tunable out-of-plane anti-damping torque.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究表明，磁化倾斜的 SrRuO₃ 铁磁层能够产生面外反阻尼自旋轨道力矩。研究指出，自旋反常霍尔效应和平面霍尔效应自旋流均有贡献，并显示面外自旋分量可通过改变磁矩取向进行调节。
papers.method_en: The authors demonstrate a zero-field canted magnetic configuration in a ferromagnetic SrRuO₃ layer. They characterize all vector components of the resulting torque and examine how the out-of-plane spin component varies with the magnetic-moment orientation.
papers.method_zh: 作者展示了铁磁 SrRuO₃ 层在零外场下的磁化倾斜构型，并表征由此产生的力矩的全部矢量分量。研究还考察了面外自旋分量随磁矩取向的变化。
papers.result_en: The canted SrRuO₃ spin source produces a nonzero out-of-plane anti-damping torque. The out-of-plane spin component is tunable through the orientation of the magnetic moment. Both the spin anomalous Hall effect and the planar Hall effect spin current make significant contributions. The authors frame canted ferromagnetic spin sources as a route to out-of-plane torque without relying on low crystal symmetry, relevant to switching perpendicular-anisotropy memories.
papers.result_zh: 倾斜磁化的 SrRuO₃ 自旋源能够产生非零的面外反阻尼力矩。面外自旋分量可通过调节磁矩取向来控制。自旋反常霍尔效应和平面霍尔效应自旋流均有显著贡献。作者提出，倾斜铁磁自旋源可在不依赖低晶体对称性的情况下产生面外力矩，为垂直磁各向异性存储器的开关提供一种思路。
papers.future_en: The abstract motivates exploring canted ferromagnetic spin sources as a strategy for efficient switching in perpendicular-anisotropy memories, but does not report a switching demonstration. Further experiments could test whether tuning the magnetic-moment orientation improves switching performance in device-relevant structures.
papers.future_zh: 摘要提出将倾斜铁磁自旋源作为提升垂直磁各向异性存储器开关效率的一种策略，但未报告实际开关演示。后续实验可在适用于器件的结构中检验调节磁矩取向能否改善开关性能。
